A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching title, authors, methods and central arguments. All 19 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification experiments, bottleneck-condition measurements, curvature distributions and comparisons of edges selected for rewiring.

after.justification: v2 reports original node- and graph-classification results, bottleneck-condition measurements and empirical analyses of accuracy-distribution saturation.

M1.justification: The described SDRF algorithm, six curvature variants, GCN backbone and corrected BFc implementation remain unchanged. The added graph-classification experiments do not document a new architecture or rewiring procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4 expands evaluation from seven to nine node-classification datasets by adding Actor and Squirrel, and introduces graph classification on MUTAG and PROTEINS. Squirrel appeared in v1's dataset statistics but had no reported classification evaluation there.

E2.justification: The accuracy comparisons retain no rewiring and the same six curvature choices: BFc, BFc3, BFcmod, JLc, AFc3 and AFc4. The added benchmarks use this same comparator set.

E3.justification: The stated random-search budget changes from 1,000 configurations, or 500 for Chameleon and Pubmed, to 800 for every dataset. Hyperparameter ranges, GCN training and early stopping remain unchanged. The new saturation analysis additionally compares growing samples, including 33%, 66% and 100% of configurations, using distribution distances and summary statistics.

E4.justification: v2 removes the edge-selection overlap analysis in v1 Table 2, which examined whether curvature measures rewire the same edges. New Appendix E investigates whether accuracy distributions stabilize as more hyperparameter configurations are included, using distribution plots, Wasserstein distances and mean/standard-deviation trajectories. Nine datasets are displayed; Cora and Citeseer are absent despite the main text's all-datasets statement.

E5.justification: v2 adds diagnostics of the stability of estimated distributions and their means and standard deviations as sample size grows. The separate 30-rewiring overlap summaries disappear. The main evaluation retains 100 seeded training-validation splits and top-decile mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting; no formal significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for four evaluated datasets and revises existing accuracy summaries and bottleneck counts. For example, no-rewiring Cora accuracy in the top-decile table changes from 63.41 ± 14.24 to 58.83 ± 16.36, under different stated sweep budgets; Cornell's Condition 2b count changes from 14 to 15. The overlap results and explicit maximum-accuracy table are removed, while saturation findings are added.

T1.justification: The proof sketch following Eq. (8) changes the matrix-square entry written as (A-hat)^2_ik to the squared entry (A-hat_ik)^2. These quantities are not generally equivalent, creating a localized mathematical discrepancy. The stated theorem, assumptions, curvature definitions and relaxed Condition 2b remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction refines 'no measurable improvements' into no consistent distribution-level improvements across datasets. It also explicitly positions the contribution as extending observations about training-free GNNs to general GNNs. The central bottleneck-condition and hyperparameter-outlier claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that saturation diagnostics indicate further runs would not substantially alter the accuracy distributions. It also interprets apparent AFc gains as insignificant relative to their spread, without reporting a formal test. The earlier interpretation connecting similar performance to differing selected edges disappears; the principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1's direct link to the authors' project code, although Appendix B still says their implementations are available. Appendix C adds Actor statistics. The BFc implementation explanation and hardware specifications are retained, with hardware moved from Appendix E to D.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tortorella and Micheli (2023) on rewiring in training-free GNNs and Tönshoff et al. (2024) on reassessing GNN performance gains, integrating both into the contribution framing. Tang et al. (2009) and Morris et al. (2020) support the added datasets. The existing literature coverage is retained.

P1.justification: v2 separates the combined contribution-and-outline paragraph, revises portions of the rewiring and results discussions, and switches from numbered to author-year citations. Most explanatory prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 expand from seven to eleven datasets and are rearranged; Figure 2 loses its random-guessing reference lines. The top-decile table becomes a two-block display. v2 adds two curvature-distribution figures and five saturation figures, removes the overlap and maximum-accuracy tables, and splits the retained code listing across pages.

improvement.justification: The added graph-classification evaluations broaden the evidence relevant to the paper's conclusions, while Appendix E directly checks the previously untested stability of finite hyperparameter sweeps. These provide a limited net improvement. Benefits are tempered by removal of overlap and maximum-accuracy details and the project-code link, the incomplete displayed saturation coverage, and the localized mathematical discrepancy.
